newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets fall.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets fall.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of September 27, 1996, were $3.864 billion, compared with $3.952 billion on September 20.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of September 27 were $15.571 billion, compared with $15.580 billion as of September 20.
It said the decrease in international assets was due to:
- Purchases of $25 million from credit institutions, partly a product of the exercising of some dollar put options that institutions held with the central bank from the option auction of August 30.
- Covering external debt commitments of $57 million.
- Net expenditures from operations of the state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $56 million.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose 1.156 billion pesos due to seasonal demand for notes and coins stemming from salary payments for the second two weeks of September.
The government's current account balance with the central bank rose 4.596 billion pesos over the period, mainly as a result of the payment of a credit that the government had given to Pemex.
Central bank credit to banks rose 1.873 billion pesos to meet the rising demand for notes and coins.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
